or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running

A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its

and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,

Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,

text:
packet-20 - unverified image reading (blind first reader)

Exposure: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or reading for this packet. I did nothing beyond the brief's rules (opened only the brief, PROMPT.md and image files in packet-20).

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-001.jpg, overview)

image-001 is a reduced overview of three paper fragments on a black ground with a ruler (top) and colour checker (bottom right). Pencil shelfmarks visible on the pieces: "Stams, STA, Frg. 16-1v" (top piece), "Stams, STA, Frg. 16-2a" (bottom right; last character uncertain), "Stams, STA, Frg. 16-3a" (bottom left).

1. Top piece (16-1v): an opened bifolium-like sheet, landscape, with a vertical fold/gutter slightly right of centre. The whole sheet carries ruled music staves (five-line staves, with vertical barlines) in brown ink, with note heads/stems visible especially on the left half. The left half is heavily water-stained and the music there is faint. Over the right half, written across the staves, is a German text in a large, fairly current Kurrent/Fraktur-influenced hand: one main block of c. 15 lines, with the first word enlarged ("Weilen"). In the left margin of the right half (running over the gutter) is a column of short words, one or two per line, in a larger hand (e.g. "Gott", "erlöbt"(?), "unaussp(rechlich)"(?), "Vnfuest"(?), "Fruchten"(?), "Eeben"(?)), which reads like a marginal list or a separate column. At the bottom, a line beginning "Gott erlöbt"(?) in larger letters. The lower part of the German block (from about line 10) is in a smaller, more cursive hand and lighter ink, possibly a second stint. At the top left of the left half: a faint line of German(?) text "...llen Was ..." across the top.
2. Bottom left piece (16-3a): portrait fragment with music only: c. 11-12 staves with barlines, notes in brown ink (vocal/instrumental score look, notes on several staves per system). No text words legible in the overview. Edges damaged.
3. Bottom right piece (16-2a): portrait fragment with music (staves with dense notes, mainly eighth/sixteenth stems), with Latin text underlay in small cursive at a few points: "et Sanctum" (upper, centre), "...gratiosus? / quia fecit" and "quia potens ... et sanctum nomen ej(us)" (mid-height text line), "fecit potentiam" (bottom). Clefs at left of lower staves.

Tentative interpretation (not identification): music manuscripts (score or parts) reused as writing support for a German devotional/sermon-like text on the top piece. Not inferring work, date or provenance.

TILE READINGS

image-002.jpg - top-left quarter of the top piece (16-1v, left half). Music staves with barlines (three vertical barlines visible), notes in brown ink, heavily water-stained. Text only at two places:
image-002 l.1 (top edge, large letters, partly lost to staining/abrasion): "..llen Was[?] ma[?] ... mich[?] ... no.." - letters after "Was" read like "mynchkirsno" but I cannot separate them into words; [illegible] for most of it. Above "Was"/"ma" a small stroke (abbreviation mark or a note stem?).
image-002 lower third, a single line of faint grey cursive written across a staff (c. 3/4 of the way down): "...f: [illegible] Mungfr[?]... ..hn[?].." - very faint; "Mungfr" uncertain, could be the start of a longer word continuing off the right edge. [illegible] otherwise.
At the left margin, c. 3/4 down: small marks "sp" / "g" beside the clefs (may be clef or tempo marks; uncertain).
Remainder of this tile: music notation only, no words. Not transcribed.

image-003.jpg - top centre of the top piece: right part of the left half, the gutter, and the left part of the right half. Overlaps image-002 at left (top-line "..Bno.." = the end of image-002 l.1, not new text). Shelfmark pencil "Stams, STA, Frg. 16-1v" at top right of gutter.
Left half of this tile: music only, water-stained. One faint cursive line at c. 72% height across a staff: "...[illegible] ..ln[?] etlichen[?]..." (reading "etlichen" uncertain; possibly "Allen" or "allem"). This is likely the continuation of the faint line in image-002 lower third? Not certain; heights differ (image-002 line at c. 78%).

Right half, two text strata over music staves:
(a) LEFT COLUMN of large dark-brown words, one per line, written along the left edge of the right page (lines counted from top of image-003):
image-003 l.1  Gott   (initial G with large flourish)
image-003 l.2  erlöbt   (umlaut-like double stroke over o; or "erlöst"? the final letters look "bt")
image-003 l.3  nachuolg   (= nachvolg-; final g touches the next column's "lichen" and may be shared: "nachuolg-|lichen"? I cannot tell if the g belongs to the column word or begins the main-text line)
image-003 l.4  cunce   (or "eune"/"enne"; uncertain - a grave-like mark over the last e)
image-003 l.5  mir   (or "nur"/"mit"; uncertain)
image-003 l.6  Vnfruecht   (Vnfrucht-, with superscript mark over u)
image-003 l.7  bare   (continuation of l.6: "Vnfruecht|bare")
image-003 l.8  Fruchten   (or "Frucht en"; large initial F with flourish)
image-003 l.9  Eeben   (or "Leben" with a looped L; I lean "Leben"? leave "Eeben/Leben?")
image-003 l.10 Kleid?  - the large looped initial before "Kleid" in the main text may belong here (see below)
image-003 l.11 (ruled-through/struck word, faint) "Lnnnn"? [illegible] - looks like a word struck by a diagonal stroke
image-003 l.12-14 faint flourishes / "Zu..."? "Lorampe"? [illegible]
(b) MAIN TEXT block, paler grey-brown ink, larger hand, starting to the right of the column (only line beginnings visible here; continued in the next tile):
image-003 m.1  Weilen v..   (large W with flourish)
image-003 m.2  Wa..es s..   ("Wases"? [illegible] middle)
image-003 m.3  nach uol..
image-003 m.4  so ist noth..
image-003 m.5  (g)lichen V..   (the g may be from column word l.3)
image-003 m.6  Wann vns[?]..
image-003 m.7  Gott wir ..
image-003 m.8  vnser an..
image-003 m.9  das Ewig..
image-003 m.10 an. Als ..   (preceded by "Fruchten" of column? reading "Fruchte(n) an." possible)
image-003 m.11 noy[?] diser..  ("noch"? uncertain)
image-003 m.12 Kleid wie ..   (large looped initial K? before "leid"; possibly "Kleid" or "Leid")
image-003 m.13 Gott in ..   (smaller, lighter cursive from here)
image-003 m.14 [?]nadigen?.. / "Lorampe"? - lowest lines faint: "..e Gnadigsten"? [illegible]
Note: column words and main-text lines alternate in height; reading order between the two strata is uncertain.

image-004.jpg - top right of the top piece: the main German text block, continuing the line-beginnings of image-003 (overlap: the first letters of each line here repeat the line-ends of image-003). Right edge of the sheet visible; a brown stain at top right obscures the ends of lines 2-4. Music staves with barlines and notes run underneath the text. Line numbers counted from top of image-004 (= main-text lines m.1-15). Combined line readings (image-003 beginning + image-004):
image-004 l.1  [We]ilen wür[?] nun von deme(n)[?] [illegible at edge]   ("wür": w with heavy ink blot; could be "wir"; "von deme" or "van dem" uncertain)
image-004 l.2  [Wa/Go?]ttes dise[?] derth[?] auchs [illegible under stain]   (line-start in image-003 looked "Wa..es"; here "..ttes"; word 2-3 "disederth" unclear, perhaps "dise derth" / "dises erth"?)
image-004 l.3  nach uolgen(n)der[?] Suechen[?] [stain]   ("nachuolgen d" then a word ending "er"; "Suechen" or "Sucheln"; uncertain)
image-004 l.4  [so i]st nothwendig das m(it)[?] [illegible]   ("das mi.." clear start)
image-004 l.5  [g]lichen vnnd Gott wolgef[?]..   ("wolgef(ällig)" not visible; I see "wolge" + f/s)
image-004 l.6  Wann ich[?] an vnns nemen d[as]?   ("ich" uncertain, could be "wir"; "nemen" or "nennen"? leaning nemen)
image-004 l.7  [Go]tt wie alls[?] vnfruchtbare Bo[?]..   ("alls" with ligature; "Bo.." or "Bä.." at right edge)
image-004 l.8  vnser an . . . gescheefften[?] / geschehen[?] will alsso[?]   (a long ascender descends through this line from above; word after "an" uncertain: "geschefften" vs "geschechen"; then "will" or "gill"; "also/alss")
image-004 l.9  das Ewigen Feur weiffen[?] (= werffen?)   ("Feur" clear-ish with long r; "weissen/werffen" uncertain; I read the letters as "weiffen")
image-004 l.10 an. Alss guete Frucht bemach..   ("Alss" with z-like final s; "bemach" or "vermach" at edge; "guete" fairly clear)
image-004 l.11 noch[?] disen da gemeich[?]/geneicht[?] sich in ..   (very uncertain middle: letters "dagenichsh" or "dagemchtsh"; "in" then cut)
-- smaller, lighter cursive hand begins here (c. 60% height) --
image-004 l.12 Kleid wie hörsch[?]/herrsch[?] Menschen dis[?]..   ("Menschen" fairly clear; preceding word "hörsch"/"hürsch" uncertain; ends "di.." cut)
